title: Japan's PM Just Landed in India With 150 Business Leaders and a $61 Billion Promise
excerpt: Sanae Takaichi's first official visit to India kicks off the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit in New Delhi, with trade, defence, high-speed rail, and the Indo-Pacific on the agenda.
body:
Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday for the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit, accompanied by more than 150 representatives of Japan's business community — the largest corporate delegation to accompany a Japanese leader to India in recent memory.

The three-day visit, which runs from July 1 to 3, marks Takaichi's first official trip to India since assuming office. It follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Tokyo in August 2025 for the 15th summit, during which Japan pledged to more than double its investment in India to over $61 billion over the next decade.

## A Partnership Built on Money and Machines

Bilateral trade between the two countries reached $27.5 billion in fiscal year 2025-26, while Japanese investment in India totalled $3.2 billion between April and December 2025 alone. About 1,400 Japanese companies now operate in India, nearly half of them in manufacturing — a sector Modi's government has aggressively courted through its 'Make in India' push.

The centrepiece of Japanese infrastructure investment remains the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor, India's first bullet train project, backed by a soft loan of approximately $15 billion from the Japan International Cooperation Agency. Recent reports suggest the project's first phase could begin trial runs as early as 2028.

Japanese firms have also deepened their bets on Indian financial services. Earlier this year, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group closed a $1.6 billion deal for a 20 percent stake in Yes Bank — one of the largest foreign investments in an Indian private-sector bank.


![Prime Minister Narendra Modi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5f/The_official_portrait_of_Shri_Narendra_Modi%2C_the_Prime_Minister_of_the_Republic_of_India.jpg)



> **"Earlier this year, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group closed a $1.6 billion deal for a 20 percent stake in Yes Bank — one of the largest foreign investments in an Indian private-sector bank."**



## Defence and the Indo-Pacific

Trade and investment are only part of the story. India and Japan are fellow members of the Quad — alongside the United States and Australia — and have steadily expanded defence and strategic collaboration in recent years.

Before departing for India, Takaichi told reporters she looked forward to "thorough discussions with Prime Minister Modi on efforts to realise a Free and Open Indo-Pacific," the strategic framework both nations have championed as a counterweight to China's growing assertiveness in the region.

The summit is expected to address security cooperation in the Indo-Pacific, the stability of energy supply chains disrupted by the ongoing West Asia crisis, and efforts to make critical mineral supply chains more resilient — all issues where Tokyo and New Delhi's interests converge.

India's Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh recently reaffirmed the country's commitment to deepening strategic ties with Japan during the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, where he also held discussions with the Commander of the US Indo-Pacific Command and the Chair of NATO's Military Committee.

## What It Means for the Diaspora


![New Delhi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Forecourt%2C_Rashtrapati_Bhavan_-_1.jpg/3840px-Forecourt%2C_Rashtrapati_Bhavan_-_1.jpg)


For the roughly 46,000 Indians living in Japan and the growing number of Indian tech professionals working at Japanese multinationals, the deepening partnership carries practical implications. Japan has been gradually easing work visa requirements for skilled foreign workers, and Indian IT professionals are among the fastest-growing groups of foreign workers in Japan.

The investment commitments also matter for Indian professionals and entrepreneurs working in sectors Japanese companies are targeting — automotive manufacturing, semiconductor supply chains, renewable energy, and digital infrastructure.

With Japan's population shrinking and its workforce aging, India's demographic dividend makes it a natural partner. The $61 billion investment pledge is not charity; it is a calculated bet on India's capacity to become a manufacturing and technology hub that Japanese companies increasingly cannot ignore.

## What to Watch

The summit is expected to produce several announcements across trade, technology, and defence. Watch for updates on the bullet train timeline, any new defence procurement agreements, and whether the two sides announce progress on a bilateral semiconductor supply chain arrangement — a priority for both nations as they seek to reduce dependence on Chinese manufacturing.

Modi and Takaichi are also expected to attend joint business events with executives from both countries, signalling that this summit is as much about corporate deal-making as it is about statecraft.

The fact that 150 Japanese business leaders made the trip says everything about where this relationship is headed.
